summary: Mode-4 track-index callback updates selected-track and playback state, then calls FUN_40394eb4 with argument 1. It does not directly emit PLAY message 0x311.
Computes a flag from state at 0x9fc15418, changes bit 0x40 according to its argument, then calls FUN_40614f30.
Calls a resident service through literal pointer 0xbfc16409 with message ID 0x304 and a small payload. Meaning of the resident service is unresolved.
Engine message dispatcher; routes message 0x304 through pointer-pool slot 0x60091024 and routes PLAY message 0x311 through a separate slot.

Statuses 0, 1, and 2 dynamically executed with payloads 0xa3/0x53. All write masks 0x30, 0x0f, 0xc0 to RAM 0x9fc15cb3/+b4/+b6. Status 0/1 execute in-binary helper 0x7a052dd8 with payload&0x3f and nested helper 0x7b1a808c using synthetic selector 0x35; resident calls are stubbed. Status 2 requests mmm_mp command 0x1c only when low nibble is 3 and prior +0x2c != 3, then copies output +0x0c into 0x9fc15d8c. mmm_mp and ack effects remain stubbed.

In-binary status-0/1 queue helper executed from the 0x304 handler. For payloads 0x23/0x13, writes low nibble to 0x9fc15f39, clears 0x9fc15f21, sets 0x9fc15f23, calls FUN_7b1a808c with synthetic selector 0x35, and returns 1. Nested resident calls remain stubbed.

Called by FUN_7a052dd8 with synthetic selector 0x35. Executes its nonzero, less-than-0x41 branch, requests resident function 0xbfc11cc1 twice with tuples (0x9fc15f88,0,8,1) and (0x9fc15f90,0,0x20,1), updates engine RAM, and returns 1; resident function effects are stubbed.
Written by FUN_60110ddc from message 0x304 as input_byte & 0x30. Semantic field name and downstream readers are unresolved.

Written by FUN_60110ddc from message 0x304 as input_byte & 0x0f. UI callback and engine handler dynamically verified with value 3. FUN_60190eec also reads this byte; when it equals 3 it requests mmm_mp command 0x1c. User-facing setting label remains unresolved.
Written by FUN_60110ddc from message 0x304 as input_byte & 0xc0. Semantic field name and downstream readers are unresolved.

UI callback selects value 3 by calling FUN_40394e7c(3). Dynamic p-code execution captured message 0x304 with payload 0xa3 when upper bits were seeded to 0xa0; with global flag 0x4000 set, FUN_40614f30 adds bit 0x40 and payload becomes 0x53. No UI label was identified.
Stores selection byte at RAM 0x9fc15719 and sends its OR with 0x9fc1571a through FUN_40614f30. Dynamic callback path verified selection 3 and preserved upper bits in message 0x304 payload.

0x311 PLAY handler. If state byte 0x9fc15cb4 equals 3, requests mmm_mp command 0x1c and stores snapshot word +0x0c into RAM 0x9fc15d8c. Command 0x1c snapshot word +0x0c comes from mmm_mp context +0x104 (time/position-like); the command return is not gated on 0x19 PLAY success.
reproduce: Ghidra LoadAP.java + DumpAt.java at 0x60190eec and 0x60090d64; bash tools/ghidra/run_mmm_command_snapshot_probe.sh

summary: Command 0x1c branch fills a 24-byte snapshot: output +0x08/+0x0c/+0x10/+0x14 are sourced from context +0x140/+0x104/+0x108/+0x10c; output +0x00/+0x04 retain context +0xd0/+0xd4. Dynamic probe confirms requested service sequence 0x19, 24-byte transfer, 0x1a with external services stubbed to return 0. Context +0x104 is time/position-like; +0x10c semantic meaning unresolved.

Receives snapshot output word +0x0c from mmm_mp command 0x1c in both the 0x304 transition handler and the 0x311 PLAY handler. The source is mmm_mp context +0x104, updated in 1000-unit playback-position steps; exact unit/meaning remains unproven.
Copied to snapshot output +0x0c by command 0x1c and then stored by engine callers at 0x9fc15d8c. FUN_680d2d00 updates this field in 1000-unit steps; exact unit and meaning are unproven.
Copied to snapshot output +0x14 by command 0x1c. No direct reader was found in the recovered mmm_mp functions; semantic meaning remains unresolved.
Builds the two-byte EQ selector payload and sends message 0x303. Built-in presets use selectors 1..6; mapping from all menu events to selector values remains partly unresolved.
Copies seven custom gains from 0x9fc15720 to the engine-facing buffer and sends selector {7,7}. The actual slider caller and audible DSP effect are unresolved.
Reads EQ selector byte 0x9fc1570d and dispatches a selected case; case 7 reaches the custom producer. The event that sets selector 7 remains unknown.

Loads a 0x38-byte persistent block and copies its seven custom-EQ bytes at +0x2c to 0x9fc1a19c on the observed initialization path. It also reads config item 0x116 into RAM byte 0x9fc155d4. Later slider writes/save timing and the physical USB path remain unresolved.
Read by FUN_40094dd4; value 7 selects the custom producer path. The writer that sets 7 from the M30 slider/menu is not identified.
Seven-byte source copied by FUN_403d4ed0; offset +0x2c in the music.ap persistent block. Slider writer and exact save timing remain unknown.

P-code covers frequency SET_CUR/GET_CUR and Feature Unit mute/volume; requested rate is stored while GET_CUR returns descriptor rate. Real QEMU SET_INTERFACE alt 1 clears shared producer state; alt 0 ACKs and preserves it. USB-controller handshakes and physical audio remain outside.
Builds/patches USB descriptor data for synthetic configuration cases, including VID/PID and interface flags. Does not prove physical host enumeration or PCM-to-DAC playback.

Reads the USB packet length and forwards it to FIFO/ring paths; 200 bytes is the descriptor maximum, not a fixed required length (hardware short-packet delivery remains untested). QEMU executes 74 seeded 192-byte packets, copies 0x3780 bytes, sets ready at 0x3720, programs threshold DMA state, then completion leaves 0x60. USB/FIFO callbacks and physical MMIO/DMA are not modeled.
Real consumer reads linear/wrapped data from a 0x1000 ring and calls module 0x10 with four arguments. Fixed-ROM service effect and DAC connection remain unresolved.
Read-pointer field associated with the 0x1000-byte USB-audio ring. External callback and pointer ownership remain unresolved.
Producer count reaches 0x3780 after 74 seeded 192-byte packets; a completion subtracts 0x3720 and leaves 0x60 under QEMU. This is software state, not physical DMA timing.

Directory-row callback requests 25 UTF-16 units into a 0x32-byte slot, formats the result, then calls a bounded converter. Long-name provider behavior is external, so this alone does not explain intermittent scrolling.
Formats a synthetic non-BOM 8.3 directory name as NAME.EXT before the final converter. Bytes after NUL may remain stale; long-name provider behavior is untested.
Refresh callback takes a context-gated path that emits seven updates from 0x14-byte records. The fsel object is not proven to represent filesystem folders.
Eight 0x32-byte slots (title plus seven rows) occupy 400 bytes; each directory request is 25 UTF-16 units. Adjacent live path-info data means the remaining page is not proven free space.

Contains the config-side automatic-index guard site compared against stock; community changes the instruction at file offset 0x1e0c. The separate flash-word bit 0x10000 and powered-card trigger path are not explained by this site.

Top-level filelist-update driver prepares buffers, creates output files, and runs MUSIC.LIB/M3U.LIB builders. This identifies builder behavior, not the event that automatically launches it on card insertion.
Per-file scan calls filesystem operation 3 to populate primary and secondary location slices, then handles tag-reader/fallback fields. The primary location bytes remain opaque.
Writes a prepared 256-byte MUSIC.LIB record including text, track/location data, and links. No play-count field is established; opaque location bytes should be preserved.
M3U first-pass scanner counts discovered playlist files; the write pass resets and increments the count for emitted records. The supplied M3U.LIB has no valid records to verify payload layout.
M3U post-record path reaches sorting/tie refinement at 0x40155038 and writes two u16 index tables. The zero-entry captured file cannot validate populated records or tables.
Music tick wrapper loads callback literal 0x40494e95 and indirectly enters FUN_40494e94; probe verifies target and return edge. Snapshot/UI services and playback state are controlled or stubbed.
Community mode 4 advances at the end threshold like mode 2; stock mode 4 ends playback instead. This is control-flow evidence, not proof that ASRC/DAC drains fade-out samples.

Message 0x90 routing reads the byte at RAM 0x9fc155d4: value 1 selects manager app id 0x12; otherwise the online-state byte at 0x9fc15663 selects app id 0x0c or 0x10. The handler emits message 0x201. This verifies config-app routing, not physical USB or audible playback.

Config item 0x116 selector byte: written during config initialization and read by the message-0x90 app-routing branch. Value 1 selects manager app id 0x12; physical connector and audio behavior are unverified.

This distinct overlay function treats RAM 0x9fc155d0 as a lookup-table header, reads a 16-bit count at +4, scans 16-bit entries from +6 up to seven entries, and returns an index or fallback. No dataflow from config item 0x116 to this table is established.
reproduce: Ghidra LoadAP.java + DumpAt.java on analysis/community/fw/mainmenu.ap at 0x40054c00

summary: Resident dispatcher switches on its second argument. Case 0x11 calls FUN_68013118; 0x1f has no case and follows the default error path. This rules out that direct event mapping but does not locate the receiver of module 0x42 command 0x1f.
reproduce: Ghidra decompile mmm_pp.al at 0xbfc138c0; follow literal 0xbfc13a34 to 0x68013118

summary: The 0x11 resident-dispatch handler calls module 0x0c, op 0x12 with a0=1 and the object's shared-memory handle from +0x9c.
reproduce: Ghidra decompile mmm_pp.al at 0x68013118; caller dispatch is 0xbfc138c0

summary: At file offset 0x96b4, loads destination 0x9fc0bd2c and target 0xbfc09c01, then calls with a1=0, a2=0x7c in the jalr delay slot, and a3=1. A zero-fill interpretation matches the known service ABI shape, but the ROM target body is absent and that effect is not verified.

Threshold helper writes control fields, calls FUN_bfc312e0, and returns. In the real producer path this executes when queued bytes reach 0x3720; RAM aliases expose ring address 0x80080000, control 0x4b03, and size 0x3720. Hardware register semantics are unverified.

Programs the producer ring address and raw DMA size/control fields. It is reached from the real threshold helper; tests also cover both format modes. QEMU checks RAM-backed register values, not physical DMA transfer or size units.

Subtracts one 0x3720 block from the available-byte count. The integrated 192-byte-packet producer path leaves 0x60 and keeps ready set; a separate QEMU boundary matrix covers empty and clock-control edges with the stop helper stubbed.
Producer write position in the 0x6e40-byte ring. QEMU executes linear and threshold-crossing writes; software wrap is covered by the separate producer probe.
Real producer sets this byte at the 0x3720 threshold; alt 0 preserves it, and nonempty completion leaves it set. Empty completion clearing is covered in the separate completion probe.

Real MIPS16 p-code setup execution captures 10 module-0x0f calls and one module-0x10 call. Two module-0x0f op-0x14 calls pair a0=0x0a/0x14 with real callback pointers in a1; combined with key-driver evidence that a3 selects module operations, callback installation is the strongest hypothesis, not proven behavior. Synthetic MMIO and zero-return service stubs; dispatch events unresolved.

Real MIPS16 p-code setup execution reaches 10 module-0x0f calls and one module-0x01 call. It passes (a0=0x0a,a1=0xbfc30d15,a2=0,a3=0x14) through the local module-0x0f stub. Synthetic MMIO/data and zero-return services; fixed-ROM behavior and actual dispatch remain unknown.
USB event-handler candidate passed to module 0x0f op 0x14 for a0=0x0a. It reads/writes USB MMIO state and dispatches through additional function pointers; actual kernel invocation is unverified.
reproduce: Ghidra FlatLoad.java + DumpAt.java on hash-matching udisk.drv at 0xbfc30d14

summary: Bytes at this entry decode to li v1,0x0f; break 0. Called indirectly by FUN_bfc32abc with a0=0x0a and a1 pointing to FUN_bfc30d14.
reproduce: Ghidra FlatLoad.java + DumpAt.java on hash-matching udisk.drv at 0xbfc32e48

summary: Contains odd MIPS16 pointer 0xbfc32e49 to the local module-0x0f break-0 stub at 0xbfc32e48.
Contains odd MIPS16 pointer 0xbfc30d15 to FUN_bfc30d14; FUN_bfc32abc passes the pointer value as a1 with (a0=0x0a,a3=0x14).

Checks the MMIO word at 0xc0080191. When bit 0x02 is set, writes 0x80 to 0xc0080400's observed mask and calls FUN_bfc30dc4; otherwise a separate bit condition can call through pointer 0xbfc3119c (0xbfc303c5). Its pointer is passed as a1 in a module-0x0f call (a0=0x0a,a3=0x14), but its dispatch role is unverified.

Indirect wrapper used by slot 1 of a candidate pointer table at file offset 0x2a34. It calls through the pointer stored at 0xbfc31610; that word contains the odd MIPS16 pointer 0xbfc322e5 to FUN_bfc322e4. The table's dispatcher and invocation timing remain unknown.
reproduce: Ghidra decompile usound.drv at 0xbfc315f8; inspect file offset 0x2a38 and pointer word at file offset 0x1810

summary: Driver-image word at 0xbfc31610 contains 0xbfc322e5, an odd MIPS16 pointer to FUN_bfc322e4. This gives a binary-backed indirect route to the setup function; the fixed-ROM dispatcher that might invoke the containing table is unresolved.

Contains odd MIPS16 pointer 0xbfc31115 to FUN_bfc31114; real FUN_bfc322e4 p-code passes that pointer value as a1 in a module-0x0f call (a0=0x0a,a3=0x14) under synthetic MMIO and zero-return service stubs. Service semantics remain unknown.

Contains odd MIPS16 pointer 0xbfc3125d to FUN_bfc3125c; real FUN_bfc322e4 p-code passes that pointer value as a1 in a module-0x0f call (a0=0x14,a3=0x14) under synthetic MMIO and zero-return service stubs. Service semantics remain unknown.
File offset 0x2a38 contains 0xbfc315f9, an odd MIPS16 pointer to FUN_bfc315f8. The candidate pointer table begins at file offset 0x2a34; its dispatcher and invocation timing are unknown.
Calls through a pointer to module-0 break-0 stub with (a0=0x0f,a1=payload,a2=0,a3=6). The first argument 0x0f is not the module ID; this call does not clarify usound's module-0x0f table service.
The upgrade AP resident segment contains li v1,0; break 0 at this address. The pointer at 0x40055078 is the odd MIPS16 entry 0xbfc3b031.
Contains 0xbfc3b031, the odd MIPS16 pointer to the module-0 break-0 stub at 0xbfc3b030.

The function-pointer slot at 0xbfc324c0 points here. The real li v1,0x0f; break 0 stub executes under QEMU and raises exception code 9. A separate Ghidra p-code run intercepts the real FUN_bfc322e4 callsite before executing the stub and captures actual arguments; the fixed handler and module service semantics remain unknown.

Under the candidate bank-5 file mapping, synthetic id=1 input caused the real MIPS16 path to issue 16 module-0x10 calls, each with an 8-byte source/destination record and flag 0. The service was intercepted and returned zero without copying; fixed-ROM semantics and audible DSP effect are unknown.
The resident segment contains the module-0x10 break-0 stub at this address; bank-5 candidate code has an indirect service pointer to its odd entry 0xbfc09f59.
reproduce: Read YQHX segment at file 0x300; decode MIPS16 bytes at 0xbfc09f58

summary: File offset 0x23fc contains odd MIPS16 pointer 0xbfc09f59 to the resident module-0x10 break-0 stub. Under the candidate bank-5 mapping this word appears at VA 0x98fc; the Ghidra p-code probe redirects that caller slot to a synthetic interceptor.
File offset 0x23f8 contains 0x9fc34000. Under the candidate bank-5 mapping this word appears at VA 0x98f8; the id=1 path uses that base plus 0x94 and an 8-byte stride for its 16 destination records.

The real vector saves EPC/RA/Cause and dispatches ExcCode 9 through slot 9 to 0xbfc06f18. Ghidra p-code consumes the real ker_init constructor output in synthetic RAM; QEMU/Malta independently executes the real vector with that recovered slot value preseeded in BIOS and verifies saved EPC/RA plus ExcCode 9 in the saved Cause word. The fixed-ROM handler body, device boot invocation, and ATJ2127 behavior remain unverified.

The real constructor and MIPS16 setter executed for 1177 p-code steps up to 0xbfc32c5c; all 14 accepted table slots matched defaults/overrides and slots 14..31 retained sentinels. The populated ExcCode 9 slot was consumed by the real kernel vector, which stopped at 0xbfc06f18. Device boot invocation and fixed-ROM behavior remain unverified.

Starting at 0xbfc32000, the extracted entry writes 1 to watchdog register 0xc012001c, calls this helper, then reaches fixed reset pointer 0xbfc045f5 in 364 p-code steps. At that edge, a0=0x9fc13d00, a1=0, a2=0xe0 and RA=0xbfc32060. The helper writes Status/IntCtl/SRSCtl/SRSMap=0, Cause=0x00800000, EBase=0xbfc08000, and 0x1fc00000 to 22+4 interrupt-controller slots. Fixed-ROM calls 0xbfc05000 and 0xbfc05028 were return-stubbed; possible side effects remain unknown. The 0xbfc045f5 body was not executed, and bootloader invocation is unproven.

Calls 0xbfc045f5 with (0x9fc2a48c,0,0x7f4); candidate clear helper has two other caller tuples (0x9fc13d00,0,0xe0) and (0x00013d00,0,0xe0). It then calls 0xbfc04635 with candidate destination/source/length tuples (0x9fc2aad8,0x9fc12000,0x14), (0x9fc2a980,0x9fc12014,0x20), and (0xbfc180f8,0x9fc12200,4), then calls the word loaded from 0x9fc2aad8. Public ATJ2127 tooling reports a Boot-ROM view over the first 96 KiB of the 0x9fc00000 address window during ADFU, making these source offsets useful ROM-dump targets. Normal-boot mapping, source bytes, and copy ABI remain unverified; the addresses could be ROM-backed or preinitialized RAM in that context.
reproduce: Disassemble hash-matching ker_init.bin at 0xbfc32000 and inspect 0xbfc322f8..0xbfc3243c; compare ATJ2127 Boot ROM window in actions_flash README

summary: With synthetic inputs (buffer=0x9fc13000, sector=5, length=0x601), computes sector 25 and four 512-byte blocks, then calls target 0x00702000 with (25,0x9fc27000,4) and ROM helper 0xbfc108d8 with (0x9fc13000,0x9fc27000,0x601). The external bodies were stubbed; reader and copy semantics remain unknown.

The real wrapper executes to three intercepted targets: gate 0xbfc10a6c with zero arguments, then ROM helper 0xbfc108d8 with (0x9fc12000,0xbfc10124,0x14) and (0x9fc12014,0xbfc10138,0x20). Native MIPS mode and odd return addresses are checked; external ROM semantics are stubbed, and first-gate ABI meaning remains unknown.
